doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Styles at the festival: McKenna and Kilgore
summary: No single name for the festival's mix of styles; Dave McKenna and Becky Kilgore are not traditional players.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: It’s great to see young guys doing what I guess, what would we call — sometimes we don’t want to put a label on everything — but what we’ll hear tonight at this festival. Do you have a name for the style?
No. It’s a whole mixture of different styles. You’ll hear Dave McKenna on piano solos, whose style, you wouldn’t call him a Dixieland piano player or a traditional piano player;

and you have Becky Kilgore, and she’s a great singer, and you wouldn’t call her traditional or anything like that, she takes more after the Ella Fitzgerald or Lee Wiley type of singing. And some of the bands will not be really Dixieland bands, they’ll be sort of like classic jazz bands.
